question: Assume today is 2026-08-29. You know nothing published after this date. Estimate the number of people who moved between municipalities within Japan in August 2026 (Japanese and foreign residents combined), as first reported in the Statistics Bureau of Japan's monthly Report on Internal Migration in Japan Derived from the Basic Resident Registration.

target.what: Number of internal migration events (moves of individuals between municipalities) within Japan recorded in the Basic Resident Registration system and first published in the Statistics Bureau of Japan's monthly Report on Internal Migration in Japan Derived from the Basic Resident Registration, for th
target.publisher: Statistics Bureau of Japan, Ministry of Internal Affairs and Communications
target.cadence: monthly, with preliminary figures released roughly 1.5-2 months after the reference month
target.caveats: The August 2026 report would normally be published around late September/early October 2026, i.e. after the 2026-08-29 cutoff, so the target period is completed but the figure is not yet published at cutoff. The count is of migration events (transfers of resident registration between municipalities)

candidates.hypothesis: August internal migration counts follow a stable seasonal pattern; the August 2026 value can be projected from August values in 2023-2025 plus a trend adjustment. The relationship is direct: same definition, same month, same publisher.
candidates.data_to_find: Monthly total internal migration counts (Japanese + foreign combined) for August 2023, August 2024, August 2025, and the most recent months published before 2026-08-29 (e.g. May-July 2026 preliminary figures) from the Report on Internal Migration. Minimum evidence: at least two August observations and the latest monthly level.

methods.rationale: August 2024 (p95) and August 2023 (p120) are the target's own August values; July 2025 (p131) and July 2026 (p246) are the same total for a fixed calendar month in consecutive years. Scaling August 2024 by the July 2026/July 2025 ratio projects August 2026 from the most recent observed trend. Shared dependency: both series come from the same Statistics Bureau monthly report; failure mode is that July-to-August dynamics differ from the July yoy ratio.

methods.rationale: Component-sum route: Japanese movers (p100) and foreign movers (p103) for August 2024, each scaled by a yoy change factor (a2, a3) derived from 2026 monthly releases. The two components are non-overlapping and sum to the total. Shared dependency: both base levels are from the same August 2024 report; failure mode is that the 2024 August base is atypically low, which the change factors partially correct but not fully.

methods.rationale: Base-rate route: annual migration rate (p199) times 2026 population (p207) divided by 12 gives an average monthly mover count. August is above average, so this understates the August level; it serves as a lower-anchored cross-check. Shared dependency: p199 is derived from the same annual totals as other methods; failure mode is that the rate is a 2024 average and August seasonality is ignored.

assumptions.name: August 2026 yoy change factor vs August 2025
assumptions.rationale: July 2026 total was 1.9% below July 2025 (p246/p131), and 2026 monthly releases show Japanese movers declining ~1-3% while foreign movers grow. August 2024 was an unusually weak month (-6.2%), so a repeat of that dip is unlikely; a near-flat to slightly-down August is the central case, with a wide band reflecting the 2024 anomaly.
assumptions.applies_when: Used to scale an observed August 2025 total to August 2026; transfers if the recent July 2026 trend persists into August.
assumptions.falsified_by: Evidence that August 2026 repeats the 2024-style 6% drop, or that foreign-mover growth accelerates sharply.

They agree exactly; they are one measurement, not independent confirmation. Use one vintage (the 2026-02 release, e.g. p13/p147) for annual levels.

Monthly all-nationality inter-municipal mover counts from the same monthly report, different months/years. Same definition and publisher; they form the only genuine monthly series available. p95 (Aug 2024) and p120 (Aug 2023) are the two August anchors; p131 (Jul 2025) and p246 (Jul 2026) give the latest yoy signal.

Japanese/foreign split of monthly inter-municipal movers. Within each month the two components sum to the total (e.g. p100+p103=p95; p249+p252=p246), so they are internally consistent but not independent of the totals. They support the component-sum route and the foreign growth trend.

assumptions.name: August 2026 yoy change factor for Japanese inter-municipal movers vs August 2025
assumptions.rationale: Japanese movers have declined steadily: July 2026 -2.7% yoy (p284), July 2025 -3.0% (p269), March 2026 -0.6% (p224), February 2026 -1.5% (p238), annual 2025 -1.6% (p159). A factor near 0.975 (about -2.5%) with a wide band reflects this persistent mild decline.

assumptions.falsified_by: A July/August 2026 Japanese mover figure showing growth or a much steeper decline than -3%.

assumptions.name: August 2026 yoy change factor for foreign inter-municipal movers vs August 2025
assumptions.rationale: Foreign movers grew +3.2% in July 2026 (p287), +18.6% in March 2026 (p228), +10.0% in February 2026 (p241), +9.5% annual 2025 (p160). Growth has decelerated recently, so a factor near 1.05 with a wide band is used rather than the higher annual rate.
assumptions.applies_when: Foreign-resident mover growth continues at a modest positive rate into August 2026.
assumptions.falsified_by: A July/August 2026 foreign mover figure showing decline or renewed double-digit growth.

assumptions.name: August seasonality factor: August monthly movers relative to the annual monthly average
assumptions.rationale: August is a low-migration month in Japan (Obon, school-year moves concentrated in March-April). assumptions.falsified_by: Evidence that August 2026 has an unusually high or low share of annual moves.

assumptions.name: August 2026 total inter-municipal movers as a factor of August 2024 level (two-year change)
assumptions.rationale: Replaces the rejected yoy_scaling route. Annual totals fell 0.3% in 2025 (p315) and July 2026 was -1.9% yoy (p281), July 2025 -1.6% (p340); compounding roughly -1.5% to -2% per year over two years gives about 0.96. assumptions.applies_when: The mild national decline in inter-municipal movers observed in 2025 and mid-2026 continues through August 2026.

residual_risks: The searcher sees post-cutoff search results and chooses which URLs are fetched, so page selection can be conditioned on the answer; only the URLs leave the searcher, and in backtests every fetched page is a snapshot dated <= as_of.
Live pages are used only when as_of is today; in backtests every page is an archived snapshot dated <= as_of.
The leak sentinel only catches registered official values in common formats, not paraphrased or derived numbers.
The model's own training data (knowledge cutoff unpublished) can include history before as_of; it cannot include the target if the target was published after the model's release.
Wayback snapshots are captured by a third party; a snapshot date <= as_of proves the content existed by then.
Assumption values are proposed by the judge model from its own knowledge, which can include the target's history before as_of; code checks their form, not where the number came from.

The magnitude gate (v2.15d) asks the model once, without retrieval, for a rough estimate; whether the evidence-based estimate is more than 2x above or below it can carry the model's memory of the target into one repair. The rough number itself never enters a computation or a prompt; the estimate before that repair is kept in judge_rounds[-1].magnitude_checks[0]. The gate is off in the own-history ablation.
